CHIEF COMPLAINT
Return visit to evaluate ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, focusing on the effectiveness of the current pharmacotherapy and any emerging symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up appointment, reporting a stable course of his anxiety symptoms since the last visit. He continues to take sertraline at 250 mg daily, which he describes as maintaining his anxiety at a manageable level. He notes that his work-related stress remains a factor, but he feels equipped to handle it more effectively. Sleep quality remains satisfactory, averaging 7 hours of sleep per night, with fewer instances of waking during the night.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith expresses concerns regarding his persistent fatigue, which he describes as a lingering issue impacting his daily activities. He reports that fatigue seems to fluctuate, often correlating with increased work demands. His tension-type headaches have remained stable, occurring 1-2 times per week, with a current intensity rating of 2 out of 10. He continues to use ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, though he has reduced his usage to only when headaches occur.
Mr. Smith remains committed to his bi-weekly acupuncture sessions and yoga practice, which he believes continue to play a significant role in his overall well-being. He has also begun incorporating mindfulness meditation into his routine, which he finds beneficial for managing stress levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to thrive in his role as a software engineer, reporting that his stress management techniques are effective in the workplace. He remains active, participating in running groups and attending yoga classes twice a week. He maintains a healthy diet, abstaining from alcohol and limiting caffeine consumption.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity mild; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, though less severe; no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed but slightly fatigued; mood appears stable. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily as the patient reports stable anxiety control. Lorazepam remains effective at 1 mg as needed for acute anxiety episodes. Encourage ongoing mindfulness practices and consider adjusting therapy if symptoms escalate. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg, reinforcing sleep hygiene practices to promote sustained improvement in sleep quality. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Monitor headache frequency and intensity, with a follow-up in two months to evaluate treatment efficacy. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue to encourage Mr. Smith to engage in regular physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue persists or worsens, consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-03-01 to monitor ongoing symptoms, evaluate the effectiveness of the current treatment plan, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to reach out to the office if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
